key_insight: A reinforcement-learning policy learns when to transfer knowledge from prior manufacturing domains, avoiding negative transfer while improving carbon-footprint prediction in a new target domain.
engineering_relevance: The method helps manufacturers estimate embodied emissions earlier with limited data, supporting faster decision-making for sustainable process and product design.
method: Learns a transfer policy that selects among source-specific models, subsets of sources, pooled sources, or target-only prediction.
Uses a validation gate to deploy transferred predictions only when they beat supervised alternatives.
Designed to predict carbon-accounting variables and other performance/quality outcomes from limited new-domain data.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 729 material-extrusion 3D-printing experiments across five polymers, with leave-one-material-out testing; mean test RMSE was 5.2 g CO2e per part, outperforming target-only training and source-target pooling.
watch_item: Performance depends on having representative source domains and careful validation gating; poorly matched sources can still cause negative transfer if the policy is not well trained.
paper_title: Learning When to Transfer: Reinforcement Learning for Carbon-Footprint Modeling in New Manufacturing Domains
